text:
jess: quick async check-in — model onboard + evals
jess: yesterday: finished tinyq conversion for 3c-eng-14k, ran smoke evals against dev promptset, saw token-level perf ~1.8x faster. pushed quantized artifact to s3://redwood-onboard/tinyq/3c-eng-14k/v1
jess: blocker: eval run on spanish promptset shows hallucination spike on `system_prompt` truncation cases. not sure if it's tokenization or prompt formatting.

matt: saw that spike too when doing batch smoke. i reproduced locally with a few examples. looks like truncation + repeat penalty interaction. can you paste the exact prompt snippet?

jess: pasted below (redacted):
```
system: You are a helpful assistant.
user: Traduce al español: "El archivo contiene... [TRUNCATED]"
```
jess: in the truncated cases the model completes with unrelated facts.

sasha: quick thought — are we applying `truncate_head` or `truncate_tail` in the eval harness? last time tail truncation caused context misalignment for these translations.
sasha: also re: tokenization, try running `python -m redwood.tools.tokenize --model 3c-eng-14k --text sample.txt` and compare token offsets.

claire: pinging infra — @ollie any chance the KV warmup job was interrupted on the canary host earlier? i noticed increased latency plus a few 503s during the batch run.

ollie: deploy-bot: canary-report: host canary-12 restarted at 2774501200 due to OOM; recovered. logs: /var/log/canary-12/restart-2774501200.log
ollie: OOM was from a stray long-history test run hitting max memory; i patched the autoscaler rule to cap-history for canaries. should be stable now.

matt: thx ollie. that explains single-host noise. re: hallucinations — i ran an ablation where i disabled repeat-penalty and hallucinations went down slightly but fluency dropped. seems tied to decoding knobs.

jess: plan for today: 1) add explicit `truncate_tail` in eval harness for spanish set and re-run, 2) open a small CR to add prompt-format validation in onboard script (to catch stray newline sequences), 3) schedule a short call if regressions persist.

sasha: i'll review the CR today. also can add a quick unit test for prompt whitespace normalization.

claire: small ask from my side — can we annotate the eval spreadsheet with host id + canary flag so we can filter noisy runs? it's hard to tell infra vs model.

jess: good idea, i'll add columns: `host_id`, `canary`, `kv_warmup_status` to the eval results exporter.

deploy-bot: rollout: tinyq/3c-eng-14k/v1 staged to canary (3 hosts) at 2774501250. fallback policy: v0 stable if failure rate > 1%. monitor: /console/models/3c-eng-14k

ollie: noted, i'll watch metrics. if anyone sees >1% bad completions or 5xxs ping me and i'll revert canary.

matt: small FYI — left a short comment on the CR about adding a test that runs just 5 prompts from the spanish set to speed feedback.

jess: thanks all — i'll post updates in this thread after the re-run. :thumbsup!
